Introduction

The TSM Supplier Import Utility was developed to simplify the process of importing supplier data into SelectSite. Since customers have varying data requirements for imported data, a standard "one size fits all" template does not meet the needs of our diverse customer base. This tool was developed with the idea that the user can choose the appropriate data fields for the customer without having to engage in additional mapping exercises in webMethods. Having said that, if you wish to provide the client a template, this template is designed specifically with this tool in mind: TSM Import Template.xlsx
Currently, the utility supports importing of the following data elements:
General Information (and Custom Fields) Accounts Payable Addresses Annual Sales Classes Commodity Codes Contacts Diversity Classes Insurance Locations (Fulfillment Centers) NAICS Codes Service Areas
Site Configuration

The TSM Supplier Import utility utilizes the SciQuest TSM Supplier Import XML message to load the suppliers and their data into the SciQuest application. Therefore, the customer's org needs to be configured to accept a TSMSupplierImport message in order for the import to be successful.
The following two items must be configured prior to using the tool in any environment:
Shared Secret created for type TSMSupplierXMLImport under Site Configuration > General Site Settings > Shared Secret

sections.title: Notes on TSM Supplier Import
paragraphs: ERP type for Supplier manager org's ERP System must be present and active under Site Configuration > Organization Structure and Settings > Manage ERP Names

Before embarking on using the tool, it is important that there is some understanding on how the TSM Supplier Import works. First, general knowledge of the TSM Supplier Import spec may help TSM supplier import xml tech spec.pdf

For any inbound supplier message, both ERPNumber and Supplier Name are required fields. These should be present for all suppliers you are loading and for each piece of data you are loading for each supplier. If you are loading all brand new suppliers, just make sure you include these fields on each supplier and you should be good. If you are trying to update existing suppliers, you should probably have knowledge of the chart so you know how to here update those suppliers (i.e. what fields you will need to include in the Supplier General section). In that instance, first update the existing supplier using either SQIN or ThirdPartyID using the Supplier General section of the tool, then load any additional data.
One other thought is you may want to consider that these suppliers you are loading might already be in the global supplier network. To find out if they are, use the .Supplier Matching Tool
Using the Tool

To access the tool, navigate to http://sqrtpwmdev8101:5555/invoke/TSMSupplierImport:TSMSupplierImporthttp://sqrtpwmdev8101.sciquest.com:5555 /invoke/JAGGAER_DataLoad_Tools.TSMSupplierImport:TSMSupplierImport
This will take you to the main page:
The main page includes options:

To select which environment to post data to. Note that although Development (rambo) is listed, this is not supported from WMDEV due to firewall restrictions. To select which type of data to load. This is broken down into the sections listed earlier in this document. The reason the data import is broken down into sections instead of being a free-for-all is simply due to the way the XML import file is structured. It is much easier, for example, to list out addresses on separate lines than to code the utility for multiple addresses/type on a single line. It is also a cleaner user experience.
Once you have made selections and clicked continue, you will receive a form similar to the following (depending on which import format you have chosen).
Each form is made up of the following items numbered in the images:

POST URL - This URL is determined by the environment that was selected on the main screen and is where the message will be sent if the POST option is selected. Directions - These screen-specific instructions identify the required fields and any other requirements for the data type selected.

- Site Options This is where the user will input the Identity and SharedSecret for the customer org where the data will be sent. There is also an option to limit the number of records in each import file (if blank, all records will be in one XML).

- Fields included This is where the user will identify which fields are included in the data to post, and in which column each data item resides. For some data types, only certain elements are available.
- Data Block This is where the data will be pasted. This can be either tab or comma delimited. If copying cells from an Excel sheet, that data is tab-delimited.

- Data Options This is where the user identifies if the data should be posted to the POST URL at the top of the screen, or e-mailed as an attachment. If the e-mail option is selected, an e-mail address is required. Additionally, users can identify if the data in the data block is tab or comma delimited.
Once the user hits , the XML is generated and the user is displayed the results once the processing has completed:Submit

sections.title: How to verify results in the site
paragraphs: To ensure the import processed successfully, navigate to . This will lead to Supplier Management > Import/Export > Supplier Import Status/Results this screen:
On this screen, you can review the results of the most recent imports. If your import does not show here:
Ensure that the log results show a 200 Success Check that you used the correct Identity/SharedSecret Check that you selected the correct environment
If the import shows on this screen, you will see one of three statuses:

A red X indicates an error. This could be due to a number of reasons but the site will not give any indication as to what the error is. The best suggestion I have is to load a smaller subset of data and see if you still have the problem, and try to isolate which field is causing an issue. A green check with a red X indicates completed with errors/warnings. There will be a download button on the righthand side which will tell a list of errors in the file. The errored entries will have to be reloaded but the ones without errors should exist in the site. A green check indicates completed successfully. All suppliers should show in the site.
If you have a green check, the last thing to do is to open a supplier and validate that the data is correct.

sections.title: Section Information
paragraphs: Congratulations, you have imported suppliers!

Below are details related to each data type that can be imported with the TSM Supplier Import utility. Please note that individual data fields are subject to change and for any clarifications, please see the TSM Supplier Import spec.
Supplier General and Custom Fields
The following fields are required for supplier general submission:
Supplier/ERP Number Supplier Name
Custom Field Notes:

When "Custom Field" is selected, an External ID box will show alongside the field selection. This is the value of the External ID as configured on the custom field in the site. It is case sensitive, and must be provided to load the custom field data. Multiple custom field values are supported. If there are multiple custom field values, delimit them with a pipe "|" delimiter
General notes:

If Active for Shopping is not selected, the supplier will default to Active. If Sync to ERP Flag is not selected, the supplier will default to approved for ERP sync. Shopping Commodity Code and SIC code are legacy fields that are not commonly used for new customers. There is a separate Commodity Code import that should be used for TSM commodity codes.

sections.title: Iban Bank
paragraphs: Iban Bank Account Number
IBAN of the bank account.

If the @type attribute on the AccountsPayable element is set to DirectDeposit, this field is required for all countries except the United States. Must be blank for the United States. If the @type attribute on the AccountsPayable element is set to WireTransfer, this field is always required for some countries, and required for other countries if the AccountNumberType field is set to Iban. See "IbanBankAccountNumber Field" on page 109 of the TSM supplier import integration spec for the full list of countries for which this field is required. Must be blank for all other countries. Must be blank if the @type attribute on the AccountsPayable element is set to Check or Credit.

paragraphs: The following fields are required for address submission:

Notes on Auto-create Fulfillment Centers for Fulfillment addresses:

This option will automatically create a new fulfillment center for each address of fulfillment type. This will set the fulfillment center's ERP Number to the same as the associated address. This will set the fulfillment center's name to the same as the associated address's name. If no name is provided, the fulfillment center's name will be "Fulfillment Center" New functionality in the site as of 16.1 makes this feature less necessary but still useful as it sets an ERP Number for the fulfillment center.
Notes:

If Address Name is not specified, the name will default to the Address Type. If Address Is Primary? is not specified, the address will default to Not being primary. If Address Is Active? is not specified, the address will default to Active. If using the Auto Create Fulfillment Centers for Fulfillment Addresses option, recommend to send fulfillment addresses before any other address types for that supplier.

sections.title: Service Areas
paragraphs: If no NAICS Code is marked as Primary, the first NAICS for each supplier will be imported as the Primary NAICS. If more than one NAICS is marked as Primary, the last NAICS marked as Primary will pass as the Primary. If the same NAICS is marked as both Primary and Secondary for a supplier, the entry for Secondary will be ignored. The NAICS code being passed must be a valid, current NAICS code.
